name: Throat Coat tea
lead: Throat Coat tea refers to herbal teas sold for throat comfort, commonly built around slippery elm, a plant whose inner bark has long been used in folk medicine for sore throat and sold in the US as an over-the-counter demulcent. [1] Singers and voice-conscious communities use such teas for soothing. No clinical studies of these teas were found.

paras: The Wikipedia entry on slippery elm cites no clinical trials of efficacy; its medicinal claims rest on reference works. [1]

card.summary: Slippery-elm-style herbal teas for a soothed throat; traditional use, no trials.

quick.overview:
Throat teas are drunk for comfort before or after heavy voice use.

They rest on traditional use rather than trial data.
quick.mechanism: Slippery elm is described as a demulcent, a coating soothing agent. [1]
quick.risks: The sources reviewed did not describe adverse effects.
